newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private health insurance sales stagnate.
newsitem.headline: German private health insurance sales stagnate.

text.p: The number of Germans switching from statutory to private health insurance is dropping, according to figures compiled by the association of private health insurers, PKV-Verband.

The rise in the number of insureds with full health cover was around 600 in 1996, after the already weak increase of 11,000 the year before. Some seven million people at present have full health cover with a private insurer.
"Of course we are not happy about these figures, since they are clear proof that the market share of the PKV has not grown," said the association's spokesman Christian Weber.

However, for 1997, Weber expects an increase in the number of insureds. "Many people with statutory health cover decided in 1996 to delay a decision about a possible switch to private cover until the following year."

Although there was no net growth last year in the number of those with full private health cover, Weber said there was a lot of movement in the market. "In 1996 there were a lot of new policyholders, but equally there were a lot who left."
However, some companies undoubtedly suffered a considerable net loss of insureds, he added.
